root_idea.summary: The root has two attested orientations: physical pliancy or softness, and a locative relation marking a point of presence or origin.
root_idea.development: The locative value of لَدُنْ is more specific than ordinary عند and, in the Quranic مِنْ لَدُنْ construction, marks origin from a specified presence or source. The related adjective لَدْنٌ retains the sense of being supple or flexible.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Primary public citation form for the Quranic lexical item لَدُنْ.
The QAC tag split is grammatical rather than lexical; this occurrence belongs under the same public headword لَدُنْ.

senses.definition: From the presence, side, or source of a specified referent.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran it occurs in مِنْ لَدُنْ constructions, including forms with attached pronouns and with a named source. The expression marks origin from a particular presence or source; contextual renderings such as “from Yourself,” “from Us,” and “near Him” reflect this construction rather than separate lexical senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Supple, pliant, limber, flexible, or soft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of something characterized by physical pliancy or flexibility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: At or near; in the presence of a specified point or person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A locative value more specific than عند and reported as capable of replacing it in suitable usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: From the time of; since a specified time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal starting-point construction marking the beginning of a period or interval.

other_classical_meanings.definition: From his side; on his part, that is, from him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction used of a matter attributed to or proceeding from a person, equivalent in the cited usage to مِنْ قِبَلِهِ.

cautions: The Quranic occurrences supplied here are overwhelmingly مِنْ لَدُنْ constructions; apparent variations such as “near Him” and “Yourself” are contextual renderings of the same source/presence sense.
A Lane pointer associated with the temporal construction does not provide a secure modern verse location, so no Quran example is claimed for that classical temporal use.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The temporal مِنْ لَدُنْ statement in Lane points to a verse through another article, but the cited passage and its modern location are not supplied; its Quranic status therefore cannot be verified from this packet.
